ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: $\triangle FGH$ is an equilateral triangle. Find $FG$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is triangle FGH, vertex F is above, H is at the lower left, and G is at the lower right. The left side FH is labeled 6x + 1, the right side FG is labeled 3x + 10, and the base HG is labeled 9x - 8. Then reason: The problem states that △FGH is an equilateral triangle, so the lengths of the three sides are equal. Take FH = FG, set up the equation 6x + 1 = 3x + 10. Solving gives 3x = 9, so x = 3. FG is required, and in the figure FG = 3x + 10, substituting x = 3 gives FG = 3(3) + 10 = 19.
